About Me

How I Work

Why I code on a phone, what I read, and how I stay focused.

📱

Working on a 6-Inch Screen

I don't have a desktop setup, so my entire workflow lives inside Termux on Android.

Coding on a small screen forces you to keep things simple. Heavy bundlers and huge dependency trees eat up storage and battery, so I stick to lightweight Python scripts and plain HTML/CSS/JS whenever I can.

🏋️

Gym & Philosophy

Reading books like Dostoevsky's Notes from Underground made me realize how easy it is to get stuck in your own head overanalyzing everything.

Lifting weights at the gym is how I reset. When I'm stuck on a physics problem or overthinking a project, getting away from the screen and training helps clear my head so I can actually finish what I started.

📓

Personal Rules

  • 01 Work with what you have: You don't need an expensive laptop to learn math, physics, or programming.
  • 02 Action over overthinking: When you get stuck in your head, either write the code or go lift.
  • 03 Learn the fundamentals: Understanding differential equations and how systems work under the hood never goes out of style.
  • 04 Ship real things: A working script beats a half-finished idea every time.
